Definition: from G227; to be true (in doctrine and profession):--speak (tell) the truth.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and Paul uses it both times to say the same thing from two sides. In Ephesians it is speaking the truth in love, so the body grows up into Christ, the head. In Galatians it is the question that stings: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? The word is truth-telling as a way of life, not just getting the facts right.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe truth without love is a weapon and love without truth is a lie, and Paul will not let me separate them. Speaking the truth in love is how the church grows, and telling the truth can still cost a friendship — Paul lost the Galatians' warmth for it and kept telling it anyway. I hold that is the test of whether I love people: whether I will tell them the truth they do not want to hear, and tell it kindly.
